      "body": "## Bug report\n\n### Current behavior\n\n`PopperAnchor` has a `useEffect` with **no dependency array** that calls `context.onAnchorChange()` (which is `setState`) on every render:\n\n```jsx\nReact.useEffect(() => {\n  context.onAnchorChange(virtualRef?.current || ref.current);\n}); // ← no dependency array\n```\n\nWhen a page has 50+ Radix components that use Popper internally (Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, HoverCard), each `PopperAnchor` calls `setState` during the passive effects phase on mount. React counts all of these against a **single 50-update limit per commit cycle**, causing:\n\n```\nError: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component\nrepeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate.\nReact limits the number of nested updates to prevent infinite loops.\n```\n\nThis is **not** an infinite loop — it's a cumulative depth issue from too many independent Popper instances mounting simultaneously. React Strict Mode (which double-invokes effects) makes this worse in development.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n`PopperAnchor` should not contribute to React's nested update depth counter on mount. The anchor element only needs to be set once when the DOM node is attached.\n\n### Proposed fix\n\nReplace the dependency-less `useEffect` + `setState` with a **callback ref**:\n\n```jsx\nconst callbackRef = React.useCallback((node) => {\n  ref.current = node;\n  if (node) context.onAnchorChange(node);\n}, [context.onAnchorChange]);\nconst composedRefs = useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, virtualRef ? ref : callbackRef);\nReact.useEffect(() => {\n  if (virtualRef?.current) context.onAnchorChange(virtualRef.current);\n}, [virtualRef, context.onAnchorChange]);\n```\n\nReact calls callback refs during DOM attachment in the commit phase, which **does not count** toward the nested update limit. The `useEffect` is kept only for the `virtualRef` case.\n\nWe verified this fix works via a `pnpm patch` on `@radix-ui/react-popper@1.2.7`.\n\n### Reproduction\n\nAny page with 50+ Radix Tooltip/Popover/DropdownMenu/HoverCard components mounting in a single render pass. In our case: a workbench page with a sidebar nav (~10 items with Tooltips), action buttons with Tooltips (~15), and an inline document editor with citation HoverCards (~30+).\n\n### Environment\n\n- `@radix-ui/react-popper`: 1.2.7\n- React 19.2.3\n- Verified in both development (StrictMode) and production builds\n\n### Your minimal, reproducible example\n\nMount 60 Radix Tooltip components in a single page. Observe \"Maximum update depth exceeded\" on initial render.\n\n### Relevant package versions\n\n- `@radix-ui/react-tooltip`: 1.2.7\n- `@radix-ui/react-popper`: 1.2.7\n- `react`: 19.2.3\n- `react-dom`: 19.2.3",

      "body": "### Summary\n\n#3899 fixed the React 19 infinite re-render loop in `Slot` by stabilizing its composed ref (released in `react-slot@1.2.5`, closing #3799). The same unstable-identity pattern still exists in several other packages' own code, and under React 19's ref-cleanup semantics each of them reproduces the exact same `Maximum update depth exceeded` crash.\n\n### Mechanism\n\n`useComposedRefs` is `React.useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. When any member of `refs` is an inline arrow function (or the composition is done with a bare `composeRefs(...)` call in render), the composed callback gets a new identity every render. React 19 then detaches and re-attaches the ref on every commit; any composed state-setter ref toggles its state `null -> node` each cycle, which schedules another render, which produces another new identity - an infinite loop that ends in `Maximum update depth exceeded`.\n\nTypical stack:\n\n```\ndispatchSetState\nsetRef            (@radix-ui/react-compose-refs)\nArray.map         (composeRefs)\nsetRef            (outer composition re-firing the inner one)\n```\n\n### Affected sites (verified against the latest published versions, June 2026)\n\n| Package | Site | Unstable member |\n|---|---|---|\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectContentImpl` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemAlignedPosition` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItem` | `(node) => contentContext.itemRefCallback?.(node, value, disabled)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemText` | `(node) => setItemTextNode(node)` and `(node) => contentContext.itemTextRefCallback?.(...)` |\n| `react-dropdown-menu@2.1.17` | `DropdownMenuTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` |\n| `react-menu@2.1.17` | `MenuSubTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` (composed directly with a state setter) |\n| `react-popper@1.3.0` | `PopperContent` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-focus-scope@1.1.9` | `FocusScope` | `(node) => setContainer(node)` |\n| `react-dismissable-layer@1.1.12` | `DismissableLayer` | `(node2) => setNode(node2)` |\n| `react-scroll-area@1.2.11` | `ScrollArea` / `Scrollbar` / `Thumb` | `(node) => setScrollArea(node)`, `(node) => setScrollbar(node)`, `(node) => scrollbarContext.onThumbChange(node)` |\n\n`react-dismissable-layer` deserves emphasis: it wraps every menu/popover/dialog content stack, so after patching the others it remained the residual loop driver in our app.\n\n### Real-world impact\n\nReact 19.2.3 SPA (Vite). Intermittent full-page crashes (caught by our ErrorBoundary) on any page with an open Select/DropdownMenu/Popover - a few percent of page loads in production, and frequent enough under parallel E2E load to fail CI on most runs. After stabilizing all the sites above (local `pnpm patch`es), the crash is gone across thousands of E2E test executions: before the patches we reproduced it reliably; after, zero occurrences.\n\n### Suggested fix (same principle as #3899)\n\n- Pass state setters directly: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, setContent)` - identical semantics, stable identity.\n- Wrap closures that capture per-render values in `useCallbackRef` before composing.\n- Hoist render-inline `composeRefs(...)` calls (dropdown-menu trigger, menu sub-trigger) into `useComposedRefs` above the JSX.\n\nWe run all of these as local patches today and they are mechanical; happy to turn them into a PR if useful.\n\n### Environment\n\n- React / react-dom 19.2.3\n- @radix-ui packages at the versions listed above (all latest stable as of June 12, 2026)\n- Reproduces in Chromium (Playwright) and real Chrome; intermittent, load/timing dependent",

417:      "title": "[React 19] Unstable composed-ref identities in several primitives still cause "Maximum update depth exceeded" after the Slot fix (#3899)",
470:      "body": "### Summary

#3899 fixed the React 19 infinite re-render loop in `Slot` by stabilizing its composed ref (released in `react-slot@1.2.5`, closing #3799). The same unstable-identity pattern still exists in several other packages' own code, and under React 19's ref-cleanup semantics each of them reproduces the exact same `Maximum update depth exceeded` crash.

### Mechanism

`useComposedRefs` is `React.useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. When any member of `refs` is an inline arrow function (or the composition is done with a bare `composeRefs(...)` call in render), the composed callback gets a new identity every render. React 19 then detaches and re-attaches the ref on every commit; any composed state-setter ref toggles its state `null -> node` each cycle, which schedules another render, which produces another new identity - an infinite loop that ends in `Maximum update depth exceeded`.

Typical stack:

```
dispatchSetState
setRef            (@radix-ui/react-compose-refs)
Array.map         (composeRefs)
setRef            (outer composition re-firing the inner one)
```

### Affected sites (verified against the latest published versions, June 2026)

| Package | Site | Unstable member |
|---|---|---|
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectContentImpl` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemAlignedPosition` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItem` | `(node) => contentContext.itemRefCallback?.(node, value, disabled)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemText` | `(node) => setItemTextNode(node)` and `(node) => contentContext.itemTextRefCallback?.(...)` |
| `react-dropdown-menu@2.1.17` | `DropdownMenuTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` |
| `react-menu@2.1.17` | `MenuSubTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` (composed directly with a state setter) |
| `react-popper@1.3.0` | `PopperContent` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-focus-scope@1.1.9` | `FocusScope` | `(node) => setContainer(node)` |
| `react-dismissable-layer@1.1.12` | `DismissableLayer` | `(node2) => setNode(node2)` |
| `react-scroll-area@1.2.11` | `ScrollArea` / `Scrollbar` / `Thumb` | `(node) => setScrollArea(node)`, `(node) => setScrollbar(node)`, `(node) => scrollbarContext.onThumbChange(node)` |

`react-dismissable-layer` deserves emphasis: it wraps every menu/popover/dialog content stack, so after patching the others it remained the residual loop driver in our app.

### Real-world impact

React 19.2.3 SPA (Vite). Intermittent full-page crashes (caught by our ErrorBoundary) on any page with an open Select/DropdownMenu/Popover - a few percent of page loads in production, and frequent enough under parallel E2E load to fail CI on most runs. After stabilizing all the sites above (local `pnpm patch`es), the crash is gone across thousands of E2E test executions: before the patches we reproduced it reliably; after, zero occurrences.

### Suggested fix (same principle as #3899)

- Pass state setters directly: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, setContent)` - identical semantics, stable identity.
- Wrap closures that capture per-render values in `useCallbackRef` before composing.
- Hoist render-inline `composeRefs(...)` calls (dropdown-menu trigger, menu sub-trigger) into `useComposedRefs` above the JSX.

We run all of these as local patches today and they are mechanical; happy to turn them into a PR if useful.

### Environment

- React / react-dom 19.2.3
- @radix-ui packages at the versions listed above (all latest stable as of June 12, 2026)
- Reproduces in Chromium (Playwright) and real Chrome; intermittent, load/timing dependent",

Done. Summary:

## Root cause
`Slot` in `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` called `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` **inline during render**, creating a brand-new composed ref callback with a new identity on **every** render.

In React 19, when a ref's identity changes, React runs the previous ref's cleanup and re-attaches the ref on every commit. When one of the composed refs triggers a state update (e.g. a state setter used as a ref, like Tooltip's `setTrigger`), that update re-renders `Slot`, which creates another new composed-ref identity, which detaches/re-attaches again, firing the setter again → infinite loop → "Maximum update depth exceeded" (issue #3799). React 18 didn't loop because it didn't re-attach refs on identity change.

## Changes
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx:2,62-63,81` — replaced `composeRefs(...)` with `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`, which memoizes the composed ref via `useCallback` so its identity is stable across renders. Moved the `getElementRef`/`useComposedRefs` call above the `!slottableElement` early-return to keep the hook unconditional (rules of hooks).
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot-ref-stability.test.tsx` (new) — regression tests: (1) attaching a ref that triggers a render no longer causes an infinite loop, (2) the composed ref passed to the child has a stable identity across re-renders.
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — un-skipped the previously-disabled "given an Input" suite (same underlying issue, related to #3554); it now passes.
- `.changeset/slot-ref-stability.md` (new) — changeset patch entry.

## Verification
- Reproduced first: wrote a failing test hitting `Maximum update depth exceeded` on the unpatched code (failed), then passed after the fix.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/react/slot` → 2 files / 33 tests pass; `oxlint` lint and `tsc --noEmit` typecheck both clean.
